newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli mother says Jordan court verdict lenient.
newsitem.headline: Israeli mother says Jordan court verdict lenient.

text.p: The mother of one of seven Israeli schoolgirls killed by a Jordanian soldier last March said on Saturday his life sentence was too lenient and he should have received the death penalty.
Margalit Bedayev spoke after a Jordanian military court sentenced private Ahmed Daqamsa to life imprisonment with hard labour but ruled that his crime was not premeditated.

"I think the court felt sorry for him. For murdering seven girls he should have received the death sentence," said Bedayev, whose daughter Shiri and the other victims were on a school field trip to a beauty spot at the Jordanian border when Daqamsa shot them dead.
"I think he'll be released for good behaviour after 15 years or 10 years," she told Israel Radio.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's communications chief, David Bar-Illan, expressed satisfaction at the verdict.
"I feel that the conduct of the Jordanian government throughout this horrible incident has been exemplary and that the verdict is eminently justified," Bar-Illan told Reuters.
Daqamsa fired nearly three clips of ammunition at the girls until his gun jammed and he was overpowered by army comrades.

Military prosecutors told the court during the two-month trial that Daqamsa carefully planned the attack after plotting for years to kill Israelis, but defence lawyers said their client was a pious man with a mental disorder who was provoked by the girls while praying.
Jordan's King Hussein paid a condolence call at the homes of the seven families after the killings. Jordan and Israel ended a decades-old formal state of war with a peace deal in 1994.
